Well, with German parents I grew up eating a lot of herring. Even pickled. Love me some pickled herring. But fermented? I'll pass. :)
I have eaten crocodile which tasted like tough fish, emu which i can't really remember (meatier chicken), and Australian possum which tastes like pork.

Alligator is awesome but needs to be handled with respect, hah, the meat I mean. Very lean, easy to overcook and then it becomes supertough. Also can be gamey, soaking it in buttermilk overnight is best. It's sort of like the flavor of chicken but with the texture of a tidewater fish.

Bison/buffalo and venison are vastly superior to beef, even grass-fed. Super lean, cooks very quick, rich deep taste. A medium rare coffee-rubbed venison tenderloin with a port/espresso reduction is mind-alteringly good.

Elk is like a gamier version of venison, but can be super rich.

Antelope is sorta like goose, rich and dark, a little gamey but without the crazy fat levels goose has.

Rattlesnake reminded me of a lighter alligator.

Wagyu is best as a carpaccio or tartare it melts in your mouth. Akauishi is a little meatier.

Ostrich makes a great burger, though you may want to mix a little ground porkbelly in there for moisture control. Sorta like a meatier, darker tasting turkey burger. It can also dry out easily.

Heritage chickens, I don't know what the breed was, are super flavorful but certain muscles are weirdly tough to cut but not hard to chew, very odd. But the flavor was roast chicken x 10.

Mangalitsa pork is awesome, it's red like beef, rich and smokey, yum.

Geoduck is sorta like clams but a meatier texture.

Squirrel is like stringy dark meat chicken that should've been used as crab bait.

Nutria/muskrat very gamey, pungent and stringy.

That's all I can remember, but I'm sure there's something I'm forgetting.
